prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a hit while turning left. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1030; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents our client in connection with injuries sustained in a collision that occurred when the at-fault vehicle struck our client's vehicle while our client was turning left. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

We request that you provide the bodily injury liability policy limits applicable to your insured, along with a certified copy of the declarations page and confirmation of any other coverage that may apply to this loss.

We also demand that your company preserve all evidence relating to this incident and the claim. This includes, without limitation, photographs, recorded statements, claim file notes, telematics or event data, vehicle inspection reports, repair estimates, and any dash camera or surveillance footage. Failure to preserve such evidence may result in sanctions and adverse inferences in any subsequent litigation.

Please acknowledge receipt of this letter and confirm in writing that the requested materials are being preserved and will be produced promptly.
